name: Salvadori's Teal
rangeDescription: Mountain streams of new guinea
description: An unusual duck of alpine lakes and mountain streams. Very distinctive elongated shape with yellow bill, dark head, strong barring on the body and a pointy tail which is cocked when startled.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Spot-throated Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Northern peru (west slope of western andes, and middle and upper marañón valley) and far southern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe)
description: A large, drab hummingbird restricted to the Marañon drainage of northern Peru and extreme southern Ecuador. It has dull green upperparts, light gray underparts, green flecks on the throat, and a white spot behind the eye.

name: Kandt's Waxbill
rangeDescription: Rift valley mountains of far eastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, burundi, rwanda, and kenya
description: Pretty waxbill that is gray, black, and white, with red highlights. The bright red rump is conspicuous in flight.

name: Spot-billed Pelican
rangeDescription: Lowlands of india to southeastern asia and philippines
description: A large pale waterbird with a hefty pinkish pouched bill marked with diagnostic dark spots on the upper mandible. The head is grizzled with a hint of a shaggy crest and the back of the neck is dark.

name: Neblina Metaltail
rangeDescription: Andes of southern ecuador (loja) and northern peru (piura and cajamarca)
description: Scarce high Andean hummingbird found only in remote areas of southern Ecuador and northern Peru. Male is green with a rosy throat and a white dot behind the eye; tail is green below and may appear bronzy or bluish above depending on the light.

name: Crimson-headed Partridge
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern borneo
description: Unmistakable black partridge with a bright red head (hence the alternative name, “Bloodhead”). Inhabits Bornean montane forest (roughly 1000–1700 m) but may be encountered outside this altitudinal range.

name: Slender-tailed Cisticola
rangeDescription: Locally in northeastern angola, southern democratic republic of the congo, and far western zambia
description: A medium-sized, very long-tailed, fairly plain cisticola. Note the rufous cap and the white tip to the tail.

name: Olive-streaked Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Foothills and highlands of costa rica and western panama (to chiriquí and ngäbe-buglé)
description: Small, fruit-eating flycatcher found in lower to middle levels of humid forest. Most common in the mountains, but occasionally seen in lowland areas.

name: Chilean Swallow
rangeDescription: Breeds southern chile and argentina; winters north to bolivia and brazil
description: Common and familiar swallow of southern South America; found widely from the coast to Andean foothills and from open forests to beaches. Often near water and regularly around towns and villages, associating readily with slightly smaller Blue-and-white Swallow.

name: Taliabu Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Taliabu island (sula islands)
description: A recently described species endemic to the declining montane forests of Taliabu. Dark, sparrow-sized warbler with a scruffy-looking, graduated tail.

name: Brown-backed Mockingbird
rangeDescription: Arid montane scrub of bolivia and far northwestern argentina
description: Handsome mockingbird found in scrubby areas in the high Andes. It has rich brown upperparts, mostly white underparts, and a white eyebrow.

name: Streak-capped Antwren
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southeastern bahia) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina (misiones)
description: Tiny hyperactive antwren of the canopy in humid forest and second growth, where it often follows mixed-species flocks. Males are heavily streaked on the head and flanks with a rufous back, dark wings with pale yellowish underparts below.

name: Aquatic Warbler
rangeDescription: Mainly open marshes of western palearctic; winters in africa
description: Small and slim with a thick, pale eyebrow, a dark crown with a pale central crown stripe, and a heavily striped back reminiscent of the patterning of a snipe. Often perches acrobatically, gripping two stems at once.

name: Red-billed Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela to the guianas and brazil north of the amazon river
description: Large, stout-billed woodcreeper of tall rainforest in northeastern Amazonia. Plumage entirely rufous-brown with no barring or streaking; note thick reddish bill, white throat, and prominent white whisker mark (bill of young birds is dark brown).

name: Alta Floresta Antpitta
rangeDescription: Amazonian brazil (south of the amazon river, between the madeira and the xingu)
description: Secretive species, almost tailless with long legs. Has a black-spotted breast, white throat, and conspicuous buff “goggles”.

name: Western Kingbird
rangeDescription: Breeds western north america; winters southern mexico to costa rica and (?) panama
description: Fairly large yellow-bellied flycatcher; common and widespread in western North America. Rather pale gray head with weakly contrasting whitish throat and breast, and lemon-yellow belly.

name: Mountain Buzzard
rangeDescription: Highlands of ethiopia to tanzania and malawi
description: Medium-sized brown raptor of montane habitats. Shows thick dark brown streaking on the underparts.

name: Brown-capped Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Costa rica to western colombia, northwestern ecuador, and northwestern venezuela
description: Tiny short-tailed flycatcher. Yellow below with white eyebrow that wraps around the forehead.

name: Salvin's Curassow
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of southern colombia to eastern ecuador and northeastern peru
description: Large black curassow with a bright red bill, white lower belly, and white tail tip. Unlikely to be confused.

name: Laysan Finch
rangeDescription: Laysan island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: A finch-billed Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Laysan; does not occur in the main Hawaiian Islands. An introduced population occurs on Pearl and Hermes Atoll.
